question.prompt: Jackson’s paintbrush makes a narrow strip with a width of \(6.5\) millimeters. Jackson has enough paint to make a strip \(25\) meters long. How many square centimeters of paper could Jackson cover with paint?

solutions.title: Convert before multiplying
solutions.explanation:
The painted strip is a rectangle, so multiplying its length and width gives its area. Using centimeters for both dimensions makes the result come out in square centimeters.

There are \(10\) millimeters in a centimeter and \(100\) centimeters in a meter. Thus the width and length are
\[
6.5\div10=0.65\text{ cm},
\qquad
25\cdot100=2500\text{ cm}.
\]
The area is therefore
\[
2500\cdot0.65=\boxed{1625}\text{ square centimeters},
\]
which is choice \(\text{C}\).
